description: Half a pond-dweller, domed and translucent, still faintly warm. Alchemists want it and will not say why.
lore: Boiled two hours it goes down to a thin green size that holds paper to paper and does not turn brittle, and that is what [[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] binds [[lore/the_chronicle|the Chronicle]] with. Every account of the worst day of somebody's life that she has ever taken down is held into the spine by eight gold of pond-dweller off a fen stall.

She explained this once, at the stall, in detail, being a scribe and unable to help it. The price was eleven inside the month. She has explained nothing at a market since, buys by the sack now, and lets the road go on believing she is one of the alchemists — which is cheaper, and, she admits, a better story than the truth.
gm_notes: The Chronicle is physically glued together with the cheapest junk in the game. Bettany's one market lesson: explaining raises the price. Good for a scene where players want something from a stall and have to decide how much to say.
